beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A wave of faith had swept through Samaria. Whole crowds had heard the good news, believed it with glad hearts, and been baptized in water. Something real and joyful was happening among them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And notice their response: they did not simply send a letter of congratulations. They sent two of their own number, Peter and John, to go down in person.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And here is the surprising part: even though these people already believed, and had already been baptized, the gift had not yet come to a single one of them.

timing.text: And here is the surprising part: even though these people already believed, and had already been baptized, the gift had not yet come to a single one of them.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So the water alone had not been enough. Their faith was sincere and their baptism was real, yet the promised gift of the Spirit still waited on something more — on the hands of those God had given authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then Peter and John did the simple, deliberate thing Luke records so plainly. They laid their hands on each believer. And in that moment, under that authority, the gift finally came.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Here is the quiet study gem. The gift of the Holy Ghost did not arrive by sincerity alone, or by baptism alone. It travelled by authority — conferred through the laying on of hands by those God had sent. Order and gift belong together.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And that same gift is still offered to you, by that same pattern. Faith and baptism open the door, and then, by the hands of those with authority, the Comforter is given to be with you. When that gift is offered to you, will you receive it?
